items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: it was arranged for Archey to take my place and I would play with the relief band.

ctx.x: And every night, I would hear this fellow saying "That God-damn trumpet player" when he came off the floor and to him I must have been the lousiest trumpet player in the world. But one thing I know and that is that they had the hardest act that I ever tried to play in a small band that had to play to revue which should have been accompanied by a large orchestra. I was asking forty dollars a week and I really earned my pay.

A very nice trumpet player named Archey Johnson was in the relief band and after a few weeks of fighting the music of the "Beach Combers", I told Leon that I couldn't take it any longer, so it was arranged for Archey to take my place and I would play with the relief band. The salary was five dollars less than I had before, which I thought was not correct, because in the other band the work was harder and worth at least fifteen dollars more than I received in the relief band.

I never knew how Archey made out with the "Beach Combers" act because I was never there until the last of the final act was being played. But Archey didn't stay in Leon's band very long and when he left, two trumpet players were engaged. They were Russell Gillon and his buddy Reese. They were both nice young fellows and both play-boys, so it was possible that Leon had hired Russel and he in turn had arranged to divide the salary in order to be together. Otherwise, why had Leon not hired another trumpet to help me…
